propositions: Operators force-close ~25 administrative-disposition tickets (duplicate/obsolete/superseded/wontfix) weekly because no sanctioned path exists for non-bug types and the failure message does not disclose the available mechanism.
The existing close-class vocabulary is restricted to {duplicate, not_a_bug, escalated}, gated to bugs only, so non-bug tickets have no truthful administrative-close exit.
Close-precheck refusal messages do not enumerate the applicable --class values per ticket type, leaving operators unaware of the disposition alternative to --force.
Write-side enforcement must reject non-bug closes with non-administrative classes and mandate reasons for obsolete/wontfix closes, independent of gate state.
Administrative-disposition closes with reasons must produce signed attestations distinct from forced-close records, and the reason must persist on the close event.
The --reason flag is force-only today; it must be admitted without --force when paired with a reason-capable administrative class (obsolete/wontfix).
